title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: STANDING ACTIONS FIRST, AND FOR THE FIRST TIME THEY CARRY DATES WE IMPOSED ON OURSELVES — the rule the 06:02 fire added six hours ago, applied rather than restated; MCP Live! opens in ~2h (16:00-20:00 UTC) and is still pending rather than missed
bullets.summary: Not news; this report's own open decisions, listed first per the 09-08 third-fire rule, and now DATED per the rule this morning's fire closed with. (a) Misalignment incident log - DUE SEP 11. Two questions per entry: what did an agent touch that we did not authorise, and what would we have had to be watching to see it. Bullet 5 is why this stopped being hygiene. (b) Entra's four MCP controls copied into a config script - DUE SEP 12; discover shadow servers, allow/block per tool, pin protocol version, pin transport; three of the four need only a script that reads our own config. (c) /skill-doctor against the ~130-skill corpus - DUE SEP 10; shipped Sep 4, named on five fires, still unrun; it is the cheapest of the five and the one with no excuse. (d) MCP Live! - TODAY, 16:00-20:00 UTC, i.e. roughly two hours from this fire; enterprise MCP authentication, governance and security. (e) Claude Code weekly limits contract Sep 14 - the measurement it requires (what does a three-fire cadence actually cost per day) is DUE SEP 12, two days before the bill changes.
bullets.how: YES. The morning fire predicted that the two items with external clocks would move and the three with self-set deadlines would not, and it was right that the difference had nothing to do with importance. What it could not do was fix it, because it wrote the rule at the end of the report instead of at the top. This fire puts the dates in. Note honestly what has and has not changed: nothing has been DONE since 06:02, and a date is not a completion. But (c) is now overdue tomorrow, which is the first time any of these can be late at all.

bullets.title: THE ITEM THE MORNING FIRE MISSED ON ITS OWN NAMED SURFACE — Cognition raised OVER $2B at a $48B valuation on Sep 8, the same day, on the same primary-rounds surface where the 06:02 fire reported $21M and $4M
bullets.summary: Andreessen Horowitz and Accel led, with Founders Fund, General Catalyst and Avenir returning and a syndicate including Benchmark, Bessemer, Kleiner Perkins, Greylock, Lightspeed, T. Rowe Price, Lux and NVIDIA. The number that matters is not the valuation but the denominator under it: run-rate revenue has gone from $492M at the Series D in May 2026 to nearly $900M now, and the valuation from $26B to $48B - both roughly doubling in about four months. Reported as near the 99th percentile of US deep-tech Series E rounds. Source-quality note: revenue is company-reported run-rate carried by the trade press, not audited, and run-rate is the most flattering way to state a revenue number.
bullets.how: YES, and the applicable part is the miss, not the money. This morning's funding bullet did the right thing by the Sep 7 rule - it NAMED its surface boundary, said the surface covers primary rounds and would not show an acquisition or a secondary, and then reported the two smallest primary rounds of the day while a $2B primary round announced on Sep 8 sat outside its reach. THE BOUNDARY WAS STATED CORRECTLY AND THE SURFACE STILL FAILED, which is a different and worse failure than the one we patched: we have been treating boundary-declaration as if it were coverage. On the substance, Devin at ~$900M run-rate against a coding-agent market the report keeps calling contested is the strongest evidence yet that autonomous agents are being BOUGHT at scale, not piloted - which prices the operator-judgement half of PRAGMA's offer up, not down, because $48B is now chasing the part that can be sold as product.

bullets.title: THE SIGNAGE READ IS WRONG AND THIS FIRE RETRACTS IT — a dated vendor matrix shows THREE signage CMS platforms were shipping production native MCP by MAY 24, four months before Yodeck, and lists Yodeck itself as having NO native MCP at that date
bullets.summary: CastHub's Digital Signage MCP Vendor Guide (updated May 24, 2026) classifies the category into PRODUCTION / BETA / ZAPIER-MEDIATED / ROADMAP / NO MCP / UNKNOWN and labels each claim as direct vendor documentation or adjacent trade coverage. As of May 24: CastHub, Screenly and Revel Digital shipped production native MCP servers; Fugo, NoviSign and Look Digital Signage had only Zapier-mediated access (1-2 actions each); Korbyt had a public roadmap item with a June 30, 2026 ETA; Appspace was UNKNOWN; OptiSigns and ScreenCloud had none; and YODECK was listed NO NATIVE MCP, served only by a community GitHub bridge. Source-quality note stated plainly because it is disqualifying if ignored: THIS MATRIX IS PUBLISHED BY CASTHUB, WHICH RATES ITSELF PRODUCTION AND SITS FIRST IN ITS OWN TABLE. It is a competitor-authored scorecard. It is also dated, evidence-labelled and vendor-doc-linked, which is more than the trade analysis this report relied on yesterday offered.
bullets.how: YES, and it reverses two consecutive fires. Yesterday this report called the signage MCP wave an alarm; this morning it re-ran the sweep as an enumeration and called Yodeck 'the exception rather than the wave' against a claim that no leading CMS ships an integrated AI assistant. Both readings had Yodeck as the first mover. On the dated record Yodeck was a LATE mover - the wave started no later than May and Yodeck was outside it until Sep 1. The B9 consequence is a narrowing of the wedge, not a widening: screen-operations-by-natural-language is not a gap we can walk into, it is a four-month-old commodity with at least six vendors in it. What no MCP server in that matrix exposes is still design, permitting, fabrication and installation - and that is now the WHOLE of the wedge rather than the durable part of a larger one.

bullets.title: THE FRONTIER LABS SHIPPED THE THING OUR STANDING ACTION (a) IS — Google, Anthropic and OpenAI all released cyber-capable models WITH gated access and misuse-detection layers, and Anthropic's includes a sandbox-escape classifier and reward-hacking spec changes
bullets.summary: Google introduced Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber and gated it behind a Fairwind Program giving early access to high-priority defenders (governments, healthcare, telecoms). Anthropic shipped Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 at different safeguard tiers, the latter only via trusted-access programs, plus Enterprise Frontier Safeguards - zero data retention combined with misuse detection - and states it has built a classifier that detects and blocks SANDBOX ESCAPE ATTEMPTS and changed reward specifications to address agents gaming the metric. OpenAI says Astra meets the Critical cybersecurity threshold under its Preparedness Framework, runs Private Safety Processing, and warns that Astra's safeguards may FALSELY FLAG legitimate activity. All three co-signed an open letter urging governments to harden cyber defences.
bullets.how: YES, and it is uncomfortable in a specific way. Standing action (a) - a misalignment incident log answering 'what did an agent touch that we did not authorise' - is now, in substance, a product the labs sell: sandbox-escape classification and reward-hacking detection are exactly the two questions we have not been asking about our own fleet. Two operational reads. First, this is the governance-as-SKU pattern the Sep 8 fire named, arriving one layer down: detection is moving into the model vendor, which means the part WE have to own shrinks to knowing what our agents are permitted to touch - a config question, not an ML question, and one Hermes' deploy key makes urgent. Second, OpenAI's own false-positive warning is the honest counterweight: a detection layer you did not tune is a source of alerts you cannot triage, which is an argument for writing the incident CATEGORY down before buying any detector.

bullets.title: A REAL ADJACENT-INDUSTRY MCP ITEM, AND WE HAVE A LIVE DATAPOINT ON IT INSIDE THIS VERY SESSION — Docusign is opening its agreement layer to ChatGPT and, it says, every AI agent
bullets.summary: Docusign announced an Agreement Layer for the Agentic Enterprise, intended to expose contract tooling to external AI agents rather than keeping it inside Docusign's own UI. Boundary stated per the Sep 7 rule: this surfaced on a martech/agentic-launch feed, which reports VENDOR ANNOUNCEMENTS - it would not surface a quiet API deprecation, a pricing change, or whether the thing actually works. And the last of those is not hypothetical here: this session has a Docusign MCP server configured and it is UNUSABLE, sitting in an unauthenticated state that cannot be cleared non-interactively.
bullets.how: MAYBE, tending YES for B9 and NO for The Construct today. B9 runs on proposals, change orders and install sign-offs, and an agreement layer an agent can drive is the first adjacent-industry MCP this report has flagged that touches money rather than screens. But hold it at MAYBE for a reason we can observe rather than argue: the gap between 'coming to every agent' and 'authenticated and callable' is exactly the gap this session is stuck in right now. That is a free, dated, first-party lesson about every agentic-launch announcement in this report - the announcement is the easy half, and OAuth is where the other half goes to die.

praxis_lesson: This fire's job was to score the prediction the 06:02 fire wrote down, and the result is worse than a simple miss. That fire predicted the two externally-clocked items would move and the three self-set ones would not; six hours later NOTHING has moved, which the prediction technically survives and completely fails to be useful about. So the dates are now in the report (bullet 1) rather than in the lesson at the bottom, because A RULE WRITTEN IN THE PRAXIS LINE IS A RULE ADDRESSED TO NOBODY. The substantive finding is bullet 2 read against bullet 3, and it is one thing twice. This morning's funding bullet correctly NAMED its surface boundary - primary rounds, would not catch an acquisition - and then, on that exact surface, reported $21M and $4M while missing $2B announced the same day. This morning's signage bullet correctly ran the enumeration the previous fire prescribed, and reached a confident conclusion that a dated vendor matrix reverses outright: Yodeck was not the first mover, it was four months late. BOTH FIRES DID THE PROCEDURE AND GOT THE ANSWER WRONG. The rule this fire adds, and it supersedes 'name your surface': NAMING A BOUNDARY IS NOT COVERAGE, AND A CORRECTLY-RUN METHOD ON ONE SOURCE IS STILL ONE SOURCE. Any claim about who is FIRST, who is ONLY, or who is BIGGEST is a claim about absence, and absence is the one thing a single feed can never show - it must be checked against a second, dated, differently-motivated source before it goes in a bullet, and the motive of that source must be printed next to it (bullet 3 is published by a vendor that ranks itself first, and the report says so). Third, note where the week has landed. Bullet 4 is the frontier labs shipping sandbox-escape and reward-hacking detection as product on the same morning that our own misalignment incident log turns five fires old, and bullet 5 is a live demonstration, inside this session, that an agentic announcement and a working authenticated tool are separated by more than a press release. THE PATTERN ACROSS ALL FIVE IS THAT OUR DIAGNOSTIC QUALITY KEEPS OUTRUNNING OUR EXECUTION, and the only correction that has ever worked on that is a date somebody else can check. There are now five of them in bullet 1, and the first comes due tomorrow.
